test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Mechanic Diesel) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: For a given tire size, according to the 205/55R16 specification, what is the tire width?
solution:
The correct answer is __205 mm.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• 205__ indicates the tire width in millimeters.
 
• The number 205 is the nominal section width of the tire.
 
• The 55 refers to the aspect ratio, which is the height of the tire sidewall as a percentage of the width.
 
• The R stands for radial construction.
 
• The 16 is the diameter of the rim in inches.
 
• Tire specifications like this are standardized globally to ensure compatibility and reliability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Tire Specifications:**

 
 
• The tire width is measured from one sidewall to the other in millimeters.
 
• The aspect ratio indicates the height of the sidewall relative to the width of the tire.
 
 
 
• **Radial Tires:**
 
 
• Radial construction is the most common type of tire construction today.
 
• It offers better durability and performance compared to older bias-ply designs.
 
 
 
• **Rim Diameter:**
 
 
• The rim diameter is critical to ensure proper fitment of the tire to the wheel.
 
• It is measured in inches and is part of the tire size specification.
